text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — after landing the per-layer partial quant change (int4 with embedding/lm_head excluded) we're seeing a 12-18% tail-latency regression on long-context traffic in dedicated clusters.
Jon: Ugh — saw that on dashboards, noticed p95 shift around the 11:30 deploy window. Any insights from profiler?
Maya: Attached profiler snippet (from bench-bot run). Top suspects: kernel selector falling back to fp16 for mid-layers, and KV cache warmup causing repeated small launches.
Maya: profiler output:
```
GPU kernels:
- int4_matmul_kernel (avg 0.6ms) 60%
- fp16_attention (avg 1.9ms) 25%  <-- fallback spikes on seq>512
- kv_cache_copy (avg 0.4ms) 10%   <-- many small memcpy calls
```
Lee: Did we change batching heuristics? I remember a tweak to max_batch_delay in the last runtime patch.
Sam: I reverted that in a local build, but didn't run long seeds. It did reduce small batch frequency.
Maya: Repro command: `./rundocker --config=configs/int4_partial_exclude.json --workload=longctx_trace -n 1000` (bench-bot used same)
bench-bot: Results: 12.7% p95 increase vs baseline int8. CPU usage 15% higher during warmup window.
Jon: Could be calibration: per-layer exclusions shift quantization scale ranges and push some activations out of int4 dynamic range causing kernel fallback.
Ira: Agreed. We should run layerwise-calib with the new schedule. Maybe quantize with per-tensor vs per-channel? Try per-channel for sensitive ones.
Lee: Also check kernel selector logs — we added a "fast-path" threshold that picks int4 kernels only if seq_len < 512 and no kv memcpy. Might be too strict.
Maya: I just pulled logs: kernel-selector: selected=fused_int4_gemm unless fallback_reason=kv_copy_penalty or attn_scale>1.2
Maya: For some batches attn_scale spikes due to dynamic prompts -> triggers fallback.
Sam: Quick experiment idea: keep embedding/lm_head excluded, but mark top-2 attention layers as 'force-fp16' in config (explicit) and quantize rest to int4. See delta.
Jon: Also try enabling `kv_prefix_merge=true` to reduce memcpy calls — that helped in past.
bench-bot: Running experiments: 3 runs queued: (A) baseline int4-partial, (B) force-fp16 top layers + kv_prefix_merge, (C) per-channel calib for top layers.
Ira: For calib, use `calibrate --layers=top4 --mode=per_channel --samples=5k` and then run bench.
Maya: Heads-up: there's a potential perf-regression alert rule that fires if p95 up >10% for 15m. We're at 12% for 10m currently.
Lee: If (B) or (C) recovers perf, we should add a kernel-selector exception instead of changing global heuristics.
Sam: If kernel-selector backoff threshold is the issue we can add a cheap prefilter: check avg_attn_scale over last N tokens instead of per-batch peak.
Maya: Agree. Also file an issue linking traces: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2842
Maya: Next steps:
- bench-bot runs finish (~20m)
- Sam to push a quick config for `force-top2-fp16 + kv_prefix_merge` and collect p95 (Sam)
- Ira to run per-channel calib for top4 and share the scale histograms (Ira)
- Lee to add a debug flag to kernel-selector to log selection_reason summary (Lee)
Jon: I'll watch the alert and be on-call for rollback. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks. If we don't see improvement we'll revert the partial-quant change and schedule a follow-up to tune heuristics.
